question: What is the EOQ formula?
reference: Q* = sqrt(2DS / h), where D is annual demand, S is the cost per order and h is the annual holding cost per unit.

EOQ
Assumes constant known demand, fixed lead time, no shortages, instant replenishment.
TC(Q) = \frac{D}{Q}S + \frac{Q}{2}h \qquad Q^* = \sqrt{\frac{2DS}{h}}
At Q*, annual ordering cost = annual holding cost.
Robustness: TC(Q) ÷ TC(Q*) = ½(Q/Q* + Q*/Q). Ordering 20% above Q* raises cost
only about 1.7%; ordering 2× Q* raises it 25%. This flatness is why EOQ works despite
rough cost inputs.

√(2 × 12,000 × 500 ÷ 50) ≈ 490 units, about 24.5 orders a year, total cost ≈ ₹ 24,500.
Extensions
EPQ (production rate P > demand rate D): Q* = √(2DS ÷ (h(1 − D/P))).
